- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk premium.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ peak, price drops sharply), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates volatility in late period (last 7–10 days); add 2–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread trend; use moving average of last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
